newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Telstra sees price cuts above eight percent.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Telstra sees price cuts above eight percent.

text.p: The Australian government's Telstra Corp said price falls following deregulation of the telecommunications industry next year would be greater than the eight percent cuts achieved in 1995/96.

"I think you're going to see a lot of price pressure. So the eight percent I talked about for last year is just the tip of the iceberg," chief executive Frank Blount told an Australian Institute of Banking and Finance breakfast meeting.
The Australian government plans to open the telecommunications industry to full competition on July 1, 1997.
Blount said the majority of competition in Telstra's markets would come from the emergence of small players at both wholesale and retail levels.
"I don't think you're going to see another large infrastructure provider like Optus. I think you are going to see literally dozens if not hundreds of small niche providers," he said.
Telstra's market share had fallen 20 to 30 percent from the monopoly position it held about five years ago, Blount said.
"It is coming down. My job is to lose market share gracefully to a point and then say 'enough is enough'...which is pretty tough," he said.
Blount said Telstra was still losing customers to its chief competitor Optus Communications Pty Ltd but that it was now winning back more customers than it lost on a weekly basis.
Blount warned that volumes in its long distance service were expected to fall for the first time in fiscal 1996/97.
The federal government plans to privatise one third of Telstra, which chalked up a 31.5 percent rise in net profit to A$2.30 billion in 1995/96. -- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9286-1435
